newsitem.title: UK: TI's results seen bearing up to stg strength.
newsitem.headline: TI's results seen bearing up to stg strength.

text.p: International engineering firm TI Group Plc is expected to put sterling's strength into perspective when it reports half-year results next Thursday, with profits seen edging ahead.

The engineered seals, tubing and aerospace group is expected to report pre-tax profits of 108-112 million pounds for the six months to June 30, up from 103.7 million pounds reported a year ago, and the interim dividend raised to around 5.1 pence fropm 4.75p a share.

TI's share price got badly trampled in the market stampede to get out of UK manufacturers earlier this month, falling to 456 pence a share, amidst fears that manufacturing will be hit badly by sterling and rising interest rates and could be heading for recession.
But most of TI's overseas sales are produced locally, so its exposure to sterling is largely confined to translation of profits in reporting results and not in its ability to compete for sales.

On Friday, the shares were trading up at 512p but analysts said that given time, TI was likely to advance further to recover its premium rating, given its record for consistently strong organic and acquisitive growth, which saw the share price at 591p earlier this year.
At its current price, the share is trading at 15.22 times forecast earnings of around 33.4 pence for 1997, according to Reuters 3000 data based on earnings forecasts collated by Edinburgh Financial.

Compared with the FTSE All-Share Index, it is currently trading at 14.91 times 1996 earnings of 34.1 pence, against 19.09 times for the All-Share Index and 15.84 times for the FTSE All-Share Engineering Index.
"TI is now more lowly rated that it has been for some time," said Sandy Morris of ABN Amro Hoare Govett. "The share may not be outrageously cheap but it's not bad value," he said.

"It is also quite conceivable that UK manufacturing has its own little recession next year and it's also quite conceivable that the UK has a recession, in which case the big international engineers like TI and Siebe have generally been good places to be."

Allowing for sterling's strength, analysts canvassed said they have downgraded their profit forecasts for the current full year to around 233 milion pounds pre-tax, and earnings of around 33 pence, from 240 million previously. This compares to the 211.1 million pounds made by TI in 1996 before exceptional gains of 21.1 million pounds.

In 1996, the group generated operating profits of 49.3 million pounds in the UK, 50.6 million pounds in mainland Europe, 101.8 million pounds in North America and 18.1 million pounds elsewhere around the world.
The company said 80 percent of its sales of 1,757 million pounds were generated in the country of origin with only 20 percent coming from export, and only 10 percent generated by UK exports.
TI said in a trading report in May that results and order levels in the first four months of the current year were running ahead of the same time a year ago.

The John Crane engineered seals division was finding its industrial markets challenging but the Bundy tubing division was performing well, while the cyclical pick-up in business seen last year at the Dowty aerospace group was continuing, the company said.
